title: An injective homomorphism into a finite group has finite domain and dividing order
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be groups (sets equipped with an associative multiplication, an identity element and inverses). Suppose that $B$ is finite and that $f:A\to B$ is an injective group homomorphism, meaning $f(1)=1$ and $f(xy)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in A$, and $f(x)=f(y)$ implies $x=y$. Then $A$ is finite and its cardinality divides that of $B$: $|A|\mid |B|$. Cardinalities here are finite nonnegative integers. Finiteness is finiteness of the underlying sets [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set].
